sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1975. South-Eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study 1, 613-664. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: Ginuman appears only in the Dagan list (2.9.5.6, 'None of the languages has been recorded or studied in any depth except Daga'); the sole prosodic remark is phylum-wide (p.622): 'Some languages are tonal but stress is generally important and related to intonation which may be quite complex.' Nothing Ginuman-specific.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. 2024 (page last modified 2024-06-25). 'Ginuman'. Newguineaworld (Santa Fe Institute), newguineaworld.linguistik.uzh.ch.
sources.note: Situation, Phonology and Pronouns sections all read '[under construction]'. Sources named: 'Dutton (n.d.) 259 comparative terms for Ginuman of Maua' and 'Royer (1997) 189 comparative terms for Ginuman of Berema (Nowata) village and of two unspecified villages' -- both unpublished wordlists. sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue 22nd ed., 'Ginuman' (Internet Archive copy).
sources.note: Alt. name Dime; 1,440 (2000 census); Mount Simpson to Naraka coast; 'Unwritten'; no dialects; 42% lexical similarity with Kanasi (Dombosaina village). Nothing on phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2017. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: a comprehensive guide, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. (sec. 2.3.1.7 Dagan)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content for Ginuman; it is a documentation-status list: 'Ginuman [gnm] 1,440; a list of numerals: Lean 1986b: 24-25; comparative study: Dutton 1975b'. Confirms independently (Hammarström's bibliography, 2017) that no wordlist-level-or-better published description of Ginuman exists; sister Kanasi is listed with 'grammar sketch: Pappenhagen 1986'.

sources.citation: SIL-PNG. 'PNG Language Resources: Ginuman' (www-01.sil.org/pacific/png/show_lang_entry.asp?id=gnm), Internet Archive copy 2015.
sources.note: 'Language resources: Nothing yet available or materials are not yet processed.' No SIL description (no OPD, no phonology essentials) for Ginuman.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Australian National University. (language index s.v. 'Ginuman', 'Dime'; author entries Thomson N. P., Royer G. & M.)
sources.note: No phonology content (bibliography). Index for Ginuman lists only 'Dutton 1973, Thomson 1975, W&H 1981' -- i.e. Dutton's 1973 checklist (PL B-24), Thomson 1975 'The dialects of Magi' (checked: Ginuman merely named and excluded) and the Wurm & Hattori 1981 atlas. Royer entries: 1990 Kanasi-English dictionary (SIL, 32 pp.) and Royer & Royer 1990 Grammar essentials for Kanasi (SIL, 134 pp.); Kanasi index adds Pappenhagen 1987, 1988 and Royer 'Kanasi phonology' 1988 ms. No Ginuman-specific manuscript recorded as of 1996.

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1977. The distribution of cultural vocabulary in Papua. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 3: Language, culture, society, and the modern world, 51-100. Pacific Linguistics C-40. Canberra: Australian National University. (hdl 1885/253061)
sources.note: No phonology content. The paper maps the distribution of terms for staple foods and associated agricultural items across Papua; Ginuman contributes a handful of unmarked lexical forms (DAG/d) in the cognate sets, with no transcription conventions, no stress or tone marks and no remark on any Dagan sound system. Wordlist-level data only for this languoid.

sources.citation: Lithgow, David. 1976. History of research in Austronesian languages: Milne Bay Province. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 157-170. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: No stress or tone content. The only sound-system remark (p.167): 'In the Summer Institute of Linguistics survey of this area in 1973, word lists from these languages and the non-Austronesian Dagan languages were collected. The lists suggest that there are five Dagan languages where Dutton has only Gwedena, Ginuman and Sona. I was impressed by phonetic similarity between these languages and Rossel, especially the simultaneous closure of certain consonants. The initial consonant in the name Gwedena (Gvede) is a simultaneously articulated velar and bilabial fricative.' Also a pointer to an other…

sources.citation: Thomson, N. P. 1975. The dialects of Magi. In R. Conrad et al., Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 18, 37-90. Pacific Linguistics A-40. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.note: Nothing on Ginuman phonology: 'The three tested as being closest geographically to the Mailuan Family area, viz. Daga, Ginuman, Sona, showed almost no correspondence at all with any of the members of the Mailuan Family, or the Magori Group, so they were excluded from further consideration in this study.' (Thomson 1975b 'Magi phonology and grammar', PL C-29:599-666, also downloaded and a full-text search for stress/accent: zero mentions of Ginuman/Dime/Dagan.)

sources.citation: Dutton, T. E. 1971. Languages of South-East Papua: a preliminary report. In Dutton, Voorhoeve & Wurm, Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 14, 1-46. Pacific Linguistics A-28. Canberra: ANU. (sec. 4.37 'Ginuman (or Dime)', p.18)
sources.note: Sec. 4.37 gives only location (narrow strip from Mt Simpson to the coast at Naraka, valley of the river of the same name) and 'The language has not previously been identified.' Survey report; no phonology; silent on stress.

sources.citation: OLAC. 'Resources in and about the Ginuman language' (language-archives.org/language/gnm), Internet Archive copy dated 2025-03-19; plus OLAC record oai:paradisec.org.au:TD1-P106 (Dutton, Tom. 1968. 'RabaRaba Sub-D' audio, DOI 10.4225/72/56FD40EBA511E).
sources.note: Only resources: PARADISEC TD1-P106 (Dutton 1968 reel: Maiwa, Ginuman, Dimadima / Sona, Mapena; note says the first ~100 items of Dimadima material 'with Ginuman grammar' were inadvertently wiped), Glottolog, Ethnologue, LINGUIST List. No language description exists in any OLAC archive.
